- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤-0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is falling.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model frequently overshoots in next 3–5 days; apply downward correction of 1–3%.
- If model forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, consider mean reversion bias; reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- If sentiment shifts from neutral to positive within 3 days, model often lags; adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead to reflect sentiment momentum.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome shows strong downward trend after 10–15 days, model often fails to capture it; reduce forecast slope after day 10.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “1.00” (strong bullish) followed by “0.00” (neutral), model tends to overreact; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent peak.
